
# LAB:User role controlled by request parameter.

![Server-Side-Vulnerabilities/LAB-User role controlled by request parameter 20260812-204911.png](data:image/png;base64,)

For this lab we are given login credentials for our users account as *username*:wiener and *password* :peter
First I tried to navigate directly to the path we are told so as to delete the user carlos but I go a 401 unauthorized error as shown from the output on burp below:

![Server-Side-Vulnerabilities/LAB-User role controlled by request parameter 20260812-205646.png](data:image/png;base64,)

I tried several options to trick the server that I am the admin by changing the id to *admin or administrator* but none of them worked 

![Server-Side-Vulnerabilities/LAB-User role controlled by request parameter 20260812-210715.png](data:image/png;base64,)

Then upon anlysing the traffic closely and the challenge was about the *user role controlled by request parameter* 
I realized I am giving the lab a wrong approach and saw the flaw immidiately

![Server-Side-Vulnerabilities/LAB-User role controlled by request parameter 20260812-211444.png](data:image/png;base64,)

If you check the fast screenshot and you will realise I tried to change the parameter id for *wiener* for *admin* which gave me a 302 not found error .
Then I saw the value admin later on assigned *false* but this time retained id *wiener* and assigned the parameter id to *true* which gives a 200 ok meanig it worked

So I intercepted the traffic at loging changed the parameters as show above and the Lab was solved:

![Server-Side-Vulnerabilities/LAB-User role controlled by request parameter 20260813-055014.png](data:image/png;base64,)

So one thing I realisedabout this lab is that after changing the parameters for the first time at login they revert back to default after forwarding the request to the server
So when the server requests to get the client id you will have to change the value admin to *false* again untill you finally delete the user *carlos* to solve this lab


### Take aways:
This lab demonstrates how applictaions fail to enforce authorization when privileged roles are controlled through a request parameter that a user can control

### Key notes~
To prevent such a vulnerability, the developer/server should implement:
1. Never trust client-controlled request parameters to determine a user's privileges
2. Store the user's role/privileges server-side
3. Determine authorization from authenticated user's server-side identity/session
4. Perform authorization checks from the  server  for every privileged action
5. Do not allow parameters such as *role=admin* ,*isAdmin=true*  or similar values to grant privileges
6. Apply least privilege,giving users only the permissions they actually require
7. Deny access  by default when the user's required privileges cannot be verified

```
</> http

GET /admin?role=admin
```
This format  should never make the server treat the requester as the Administrator

The Server should have an authorization procedure like this:
```
Request
   ↓
Identify authenticated user
   ↓
Retrieve user's role from trusted server-side state
   ↓
Is user authorized?
      ↙       ↘
    YES        NO
     ↓          ↓
  Allow       403
```
